rv.q: Director, writer and actor Phelim McDermott's musing on creativity and his relationship with composer Philip Glass and his music strikes me as quite beautiful, but some will find it exasperating.
Tao of Glass overflows with generosity and spirituality.
Fortunately, for the most part, it also happens to be bloody marvellous.
In the second half, after a couple of, admittedly, excellent digressions, we discover that nothing is to be done, because as it turns out, all is well.
'Tao of Glass' review — Phelim McDermott is totally enthralling in this love letter to Philip Glass and theatre Read our review of Tao of Glass , now in performances at @sohoplace to 12 September.
At times magical, beautiful and wonderful, Tao of Glass is a show like no other and one that deserves to be seen to be believed.

A small but beautifully formed band with Percussion (Chris Vatalaro), Piano (Catherine Tinker), Clarinet (Jack McNeill and Violin (Kasia Ziminska) performed the ten works brilliantly (with the help of a fantastic and covetable Steinway Spirio player piano). Sound throughout was perfectly managed, with recordings, voice and live music.

cn.t: McDermott's quasi-mystical exploration of creativity and Philip Glass divides critics, with most finding it beautiful and enthralling despite its pretension. The charming first half enchants more than the uneven second.
